reviews.review:
I'm writing this review having just finished the game, and I can wholehartedly say that I enjoyed nearly every moment of it. If you are looking for a great popcorn game full of hacking, slashing, shooting, and generally great gory time, this one is one of the best. It isn't particularly long, but it never overstays its welcome or feels the need to bloat its length with meaningless fluff. 
As a Warhammer game, it excels. I highly recomend that if anyone is even remotely interested in the Warhammer 40k universe that they pick this up. It won't beat you over the head with the mountains of lore, but will do a great job introducing you to the setting, from the cathedral-like manufactorums, to the bombed out hive cities. The Space Marines are properly zealous, the imperial guard is appropriately dying like flies, the orks are just orky enough, and the inquistion is still a collection of massive bellends. Bolters roar, chainswords shred, the armor feels and sounds like the two ton piece of art that it is. 

All in all, I give this game a 8.75/10. The main things holding it back are the occasionally stilted writing, and the speed at which you die. Lategame, swarms of enemies start packing lots, and lots, of Lasguns. In lore, a lasgun is about as effective against space marine armor as a slingshot against plate mail, but these little bastards will shred you faster than a Tyranid swarm through a PDF. As such, the late game can be... frustrating, requiring you to spend most of your fight hiding behind cover and taking potshots like a filthy Tau. In addition, the final boss is disapointing. Instead of a grand 1v1, you fight four waves of enemies, and then take down the boss in a button mashing QTE. This is made all the more disapointing as the game already provided a servicable, if not particulalry spectacular, boss fight in the last chapter. Overall though, I found the game to be good fun, and well worth the money I spent on it.

Oh, and PRAISE THE EMPEROR!

Fun game, and for cheap the campaign plays well. Negative review because multiplayer has 3 maps and there is a lot of content stuck behind dlc paywalls. There isn't enough content in the multiplayer as it is, so I would like to play the dlc maps and gamemode. I could buy it, but I shouldn't have to considering the multiplayer feels incomplete.

DO NOT BUY FULL PRICE. 


The Anniversary Edition isn't any kind of graphical remaster, its just a monstrous cash grab preying on unsuspecting customers. They've just shoved in the DLC which is just for multiplayer and tripled the price. So first time buyers are now  just being forced to buy 
 all the DLC rather than pick and choose what stuff they want. The multiplayer has at most maybe 250 players on a good day so good luck even getting a game in your region.

They did give the Anniversary Edition as a free upgrade for everyone that owns the game already which is neat but they sure as hell shouldn't be charging triple the price for it, not worth it. 

Space Marine is still one of the best Warhammer 40,000 games ever made. The campaign is only about 5 hours long but it is excellent, if you can muster up three mates the coop survival mode Exterminatus is excellent and if you can find a whole bunch of mates the PVP multiplayer options are also excellent. I highly recommend the game just not the ♥♥♥♥♥♥ cash grab Anniversary Edition

As a fan of Space Marine, and a fan of the 40k universe in general, it's just really disappointing that they didn't put in some effort for the Anniversary Edition with a proper remaster with at least updated graphics and some tweaking to the multiplayer lobby and progression.

Still recommend because the game is excellent just wait until its WAY WAY WAY cheaper to buy it.

Basically what W40K:Space Marine is, is take the Ripping, tearing, bloodshed, destruction and annihilation from Doom, and slap a Warhammer:40K skin on it and change the POV to thirdperson.

[spoiler](ps: having the jump pack and the thunder hammer is probably one of the best points of the game so just keep that in mind)[/spoiler]
Be the greatest of the Emperor of Mankind's warriors in one of the most accurate and intense portrayals of the Adeptus Astartes and the 40k universe that you've always wanted to be.
